summary: Memory-floor case: the baseline already reads and writes every element exactly once (83.9 MB each way) and sits at headroom 1.06-1.08, so 1.5x is not reachable; the shipped state 585cffcc3a1ab1fa is 1.046x over the baseline (240 pairs, CI 1.041-1.049, 47.4 us vs 49.5 us), leaving headroom 1.02. amdclang issues the 8 global_load_dwordx4 of the 4 heads only after ~1000 instructions of powf/sincosf; the winning state computes the source addresses and issues all 8 loads at the top of the kernel, before the wait for pos_ids (weakened to vmcnt(8)) and before the pow/sincos math, into registers the kernel never used (v56..v87), with the head index clamped to total-1 so the speculative loads stay in bounds on tail head groups. The final rotation keeps amdclang's operation order (v_pk_mul then v_pk_fma), so results are bit-identical; no source state was made.

friction: edit text takes instructions only: a new label / block cannot be introduced by `edit` (only by edit_ir of a 1900-instruction body). I wanted a guarded block `if nh == 4 { loads }` and instead had to make the speculative loads safe by clamping the head index (s_min_u32) - worked here, but is not always possible.

No 'hoist loads' transform: moving a load group above a long ALU region meant rewriting the address computation by hand with fresh registers and renaming the consumers. A transform `hoist_loads(block, to=block[index])` that re-materializes the address chain into never-named registers would have done state d50cfcf3 in one call.
static_check was run on the wrong (parent) id by my own mistake after a follow-up edit; an edit result that echoed 'static: not yet checked' or auto-ran the static check would save a round trip.

The dst-address vectors of Lft21 are only identified by reading 220 instructions; a def-use query ('which register holds the address used by store N, and where is it defined') would make such renames safer - my first edit mapped two stores to the wrong address registers and only careful rereading caught it before check.

liveness lists `dead_across_block` SGPRs up to s101 although features says 71 SGPRs are used; it was unclear whether SGPRs above the kernel's count are free to use (they were: the descriptor followed the code).
lessons: fi_rope (headroom 1.06-1.08, each element touched once): amdclang places the data loads after ~1000 instructions of powf/sincosf even though the addresses depend only on arguments and thread ids. Issuing all 8 global_load_dwordx4 first and doing the transcendental math while they are in flight gave 1.037x (240 pairs); also overlapping them with the pos_ids load (vmcnt(8) instead of vmcnt(0)) added 0.5% (parity on its own), 1.046x total, headroom 1.02.

A probe that removed the pow/sincos math entirely from the hoisted state timed the same (48.16 vs 48.14 us): once loads are in flight, ~1000 VALU instructions per wave are free at this size; before hoisting, the same math cost about 2 us of 50. Check with such a probe before trimming arithmetic.

Look for 'long ALU prologue, then loads' in any amdclang build with libm calls (powf, sincosf, expf): hoisting loads above the math is a bit-identical edit worth a few percent even at the memory floor.
Speculative hoisted loads can be made safe without a branch by clamping the index with s_min_u32 to the last valid row; the duplicate load on tail groups is harmless.
coarsen factor 2 on a 1-wave workgroup that moves 8 KB lost 2.7% again (0.973) on the hoisted state, as it did on the baseline: do not retry coarsen on kernels whose waves already move several KB.
Registers never named by amdclang (v56+ here) are free for hoisted load destinations: 56 -> 96 VGPRs did not change occupancy (limiter stays hardware).

session.final:
`fi_rope` is at the memory floor, so the 1.5x target was out of reach; the shipped state `585cffcc3a1ab1fa` is a verified 1.046x over the baseline (95 % CI 1.041–1.049, 240 pairs, 47.4 µs against 49.5 µs). It passes the static check and the full battery (98/98), and the report is recorded.

- **Why 1.5x is not possible:** the baseline already reads and writes each element exactly once (83.9 MB each way) at headroom 1.06–1.08. The shipped state leaves headroom 1.02.
- **What the win does:** amdclang issues the 8 data loads for the 4 heads only after about 1000 instructions of `powf`/`sincosf`. The shipped state computes the addresses and issues those loads at the top of the kernel, so they are in flight during the math. The rotation keeps amdclang's operation order.
- **Second step, on its own parity:** issuing the data loads before the wait on `pos_ids` as well added 0.5 % over the first hoisted state (CI 1.000–1.011). The first hoisted state alone measured 1.037x.
- **Tail groups:** the hoisted loads are speculative, so the head index is clamped to the last valid head to keep them in bounds when a group has fewer than 4 heads.
- **What did not pay:**
  - `coarsen` factor 2 on the hoisted state lost 2.7 %.
  - A diagnostic probe with the `pow`/`sincos` math removed timed the same (48.16 µs against 48.14 µs), so trimming arithmetic cannot help further.

I stopped after those three follow-ups each brought under 1 %. No source-level variant was made, so the whole gain is at the machine level.
